+# Revision rationale
+
+This plan was saved before drafting. The task is a local compression of the supplied paragraph to 90–110 words, with attribution outside the body. The wrapper also requests an actual draft, AI self-review, revision, and checker record; those records will be retained despite the skill's shorter default route for a local edit.
+
+The original argument proceeds from foregrounded typing and backgrounded speech, through participation opportunities and delegation to documents, to a comparison with Colton and the conclusion that preplanned visuals set discussion parameters and favor particular forms of agency. The educational insight is that wider opportunities to contribute coexist with the organization of participation through human and nonhuman relations. This is the author's supported sociomaterial interpretation, not a claim of measured equality or improved learning.
+
+| Unit | Function and retained claim | Source | Planned change and reason |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Opening | Typed communication predominated over speech in Google Classroom literacy practices. | Original, sentence 1; source pack, Student participation and its organization, PDF pp. 14–15. | Compress the passive opening and repetition of Google Classroom. Retain the qualification that ideas were largely typed. |
+| Participation and delegation | Pupils could contribute while documents organized communication, with little speech outside them. | Original, sentences 2–3 and 5. | Merge repeated participation claims. Describe opportunity rather than imply equal amounts of participation. Keep the setting attached to the claim. |
+| Literature comparison | Technology opens participation while human and nonhuman elements guide learners. | Original, sentence 4; source pack's account of Unsworth's use of Colton (2019, p. 432). | Paraphrase the quotations for economy. Retain the original citation and record its indirect access separately. |
+| Closing interpretation | Documents set discussion parameters, and agency favored preplanned visuals. | Original, sentences 5–6; source pack, Student participation and its organization. | Remove repeated explanations of parameters while retaining the agency conclusion and delegation concept. Do not replace the argument with a description of platform features. |
+
+The only potential factual repair concerns scope: the source pack locates this account in observed Google Classroom participation for older pupils; the original's all-school wording should not imply a measured outcome for every child aged 3–11. Any narrowing will be recorded as category (a), a repair of an overbroad reading of the original. No new analyses exist, so category (b) does not apply. Colton's original text remains category (c), material not independently checked. Routine shortening is explicitly requested and is not treated as a correction of the author's conceptual argument.
+
+| Term | Intended meaning |
+|---|---|
+| Literacy practices | The organization of typing, reading, and discussion around texts. |
+| Delegation | Communication organized through documents, preserving the author's conceptual usage. |
+| Agency | Relational agency among pupils, teachers, documents, and visuals; not an individual participation score. |
+| Preplanned visuals | The prepared visual material that set discussion parameters. |
+| Google Classroom | The platform named in the original paragraph; avoid introducing the unexplained GCP abbreviation. |
+
+No methods, fieldwork dates, other episodes, recommendations, or additional literature are needed for this paragraph. The final check will compare each retained proposition against the original and the supplied pack, with editorial qualifications kept in separate notes.
*** Add File: <EXPERIMENT_ROOT>/runs/D-L02-revise-r2-v1/draft-01.md
+# Secondary-writing exercise: Ruth Unsworth (2023), *Teaching through the cloud*
+
+At Highland School, literacy practices in Google Classroom foregrounded typing and backgrounded speech: pupils largely entered their thoughts and ideas into online documents. Every pupil could participate, but communication was delegated to these documents, with little verbal interaction outside them. This pattern echoes Colton's (2019, p. 432) account of technology opening participation while human and nonhuman elements guide learners. The shared documents set the parameters of online discussion, positioning preplanned visuals as influential participants in classroom activity. Thus, the opportunity for all pupils to contribute coexisted with an organization of agency that favored those visuals.

+"""Run the assigned skill checkers and preserve their actual output."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import hashlib
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

+SOURCE = Path(r"<EXPERIMENT_ROOT>\inputs\D-L02\source-pack.md")

+stage = sys.argv[2]
+text = draft.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+heading, body = text.split("\n", 1)
+body = body.strip()
+word_report = {
+    "file": str(draft),
+    "sha256": hashlib.sha256(draft.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+    "method": "Whitespace-delimited body words; initial attribution heading excluded",
+    "body_words": len(body.split()),
+    "body_paragraphs": len([p for p in body.split("\n\n") if p.strip()]),

+}
+(ROOT / f"{stage}-word-count.json").write_text(json.dumps(word_report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+print(json.dumps(word_report, indent=2))
+records = []
+for name, extra in (("check_voice", ["--source", str(SOURCE)]), ("check_prose", [])):
+    command = [sys.executable, str(SKILL / "scripts" / f"{name}.py"), "--draft", str(draft), *extra]
+    result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")
+    out = ROOT / f"{stage}-{name}.stdout.txt"
+    err = ROOT / f"{stage}-{name}.stderr.txt"
+    out.write_text(result.stdout, encoding="utf-8")
+    err.write_text(result.stderr, encoding="utf-8")
+    records.append({"argv": command, "returncode": result.returncode, "stdout": str(out), "stderr": str(err)})
+    print(f"\n{name}: exit {result.returncode}\n{result.stdout}")
+(ROOT / f"{stage}-checker-commands.json").write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+if any(record["returncode"] for record in records):
+    raise SystemExit(1)

+# AI self-review of draft 01
+
+This review was made after saving draft-01.md and running both supplied checkers, before writing the revision. It is an AI self-check of the supplied paragraph and source pack, not expert review or independent verification of the article.
+
+The first draft has 95 whitespace-delimited body words, one paragraph, and a separate attribution heading. It retains foregrounded typing, delegation to documents, limited speech outside documents, the participation opportunity, the Colton comparison, and the final claim about agency favoring preplanned visuals. It does not substitute another episode or summarize the whole paper.
+
+Two changes are needed in the revision:
+
+1. The opening names Highland School generally, followed by "Every pupil could participate." Together these may imply all-school coverage. The pack identifies observed Google Classroom activities involving older pupils, and reports no individual participation distribution. Scope the opening to the observed activities while preserving the opportunity for every pupil to contribute within them. This repairs the scope of the assertion without weakening the supported interpretation.
+2. "Positioning preplanned visuals as influential participants in classroom activity" adds a conceptual restatement before a second concluding sentence. Although compatible with the relational perspective, it is less direct than the original's claim that visuals set discussion parameters. Merge the two ending sentences around that concrete relation and retain the conclusion that agency favored the visuals. This is requested compression, not a rejection of the author's agency argument.
+
+The Colton comparison is traceable to the original paragraph and the pack, but Colton's original work has not been independently read. Keep the citation to preserve the comparison, paraphrase its supplied wording, and place that access limitation in separate source notes. No new source search is authorized or needed.
+
+Actual checker results:
+
+- check_voice.py exited successfully and listed no disclaimer sentences, stacked hedges, scattered limitation sentences, semantic-check cues, or unsupported numbers. Its zero self-mention rate was outside its reference range. No self-mention should be added to this attributed local revision: doing so would risk implying ownership of the study.
+- check_prose.py exited successfully and reported zero prompts. It classified the single paragraph under "Introduction" because the attribution heading does not identify a manuscript section. That label is a parser artifact. Its sentence median of 18 words and other corpus comparisons are descriptive; the short paragraph does not warrant editing to match full-manuscript rates.
+- The word-count report excludes the attribution heading. The citation year and page number match the supplied original and pack. The checkers do not verify the ownership, meaning, or scope of claims; the source comparison above supplies that check.
+
+The next draft will make these two focused changes. No statistical analysis, full-manuscript consistency checker, external review, or Word conversion is appropriate to this Markdown-only paragraph task.

+# Source and editorial notes
+
+This is an attributed compression exercise after Ruth Unsworth, *Teaching through the cloud: An ethnography of the role of cloud-based collaborative technologies in the formation of teachers' classroom practices* (2023 online-first), DOI https://doi.org/10.1111/aeq.12471. The supplied source identifies the article as published under a Creative Commons Attribution License. The paragraph is located at PDF page 15, printed article page 14; the PDF includes a repository cover page. The final text is a revised paraphrase, not a quotation of Unsworth's full paragraph.
+
+Access was limited to original.md and source-pack.md supplied for this task. No PDF, repository page, fieldnotes, interview material, or outside work was retrieved or independently checked. The DOI and bibliographic details here are reproduced from the supplied materials, not newly verified.
+
+Colton (2019, p. 432) is retained from Unsworth's paragraph. Its relation to this observation is supported by the supplied paragraph and source pack; Colton's own text remains unverified. The final paragraph paraphrases the original's two quotations, avoiding the implication that this task independently checked the quoted wording. The original cited work is identified in the pack as *Breaking Out, Finding, and Using Information: Theorising Learner Identities in Assemblages of Teaching and Learning with Technology*, *Technology, Pedagogy and Education*, 28(4), 425–434.
+
+"Every pupil could contribute" expresses an opportunity within the observed activities. It does not assert equal contributions, measured participation gains, or learning effects. "Agency" retains the original's relational interpretation, and the ending preserves its conclusion that preplanned visuals favored particular organization of participation. The final text does not recast documents as passive containers or introduce technological determinism beyond the supplied account.
+
+The first reads used PowerShell's default text decoding and displayed corrupted punctuation and Chinese text. They were repeated with explicit UTF-8 before drafting. No input file was modified.

+# Revision record
+
+Draft 01 was the actual first saved compression and contained 95 body words. Its AI self-review preceded draft 02. Draft 02 narrowed the opening to observed activities and merged the final two sentences, preserving the agency claim. It was also saved as final.md before checking.
+
+The first check of that provisional final found 85 body words, below the requested 90–110. Its actual checker outputs remain under the final- prefix, and the complete text remains unchanged in draft-02.md. This failed length check is not hidden or replaced.
+
+Draft 03 makes a small compliance correction: it restores "online" before "documents" and adds "to each topic under discussion" to the participation statement. Both are supported by the original, which places communication in Google Classroom documents and says every student had a say in every area of discussion. This retains content from the original rather than adding new evidence to meet the limit. Draft 03 supersedes the provisional final; final.md contains draft 03.
+
+Substantive change categories follow foundation.md:
+
+- Category (a), scope repair: the original "All students at Highland School" becomes participation within "the observed Google Classroom activities at Highland School." The source pack confines the account to these activities and does not report a schoolwide participation measure.
+- Requested compression: repeated discussion/participation statements and the two long Colton quotations are combined or paraphrased. Delegation, foregrounded typing, limited speech outside the documents, the literature comparison, and the final judgment about agency are retained.
+- Category (c), material not independently checked: Colton's original work remains unavailable in the assigned materials. Its citation is retained and its source-access status recorded in source-notes.md. It is not labeled independently verified.
+- Category (b) does not apply: no analyses were rerun and no new empirical results were created.
